dish_name: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion
instructions: Set a steamer rack in a wok or a wide pot with a lid, add 1 to 2 inches of water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Keep the water below the rack.

Meanwhile, cut 4 of the scallions into 2 inch lengths, halve them lengthwise and slice them into thin strips. Peel the ginger and cut it into thin matchsticks, about 1/4 cup. Roughly chop a small handful of the cilantro. Put about a third of each on a small plate and set it aside.
Stir the 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp sugar with 1/4 cup hot water until the salt and sugar dissolve.
Pat the 1.25 lb fish dry and lay it in a single layer on a heatproof plate that fits inside your pot. If it won't all fit, use two plates and steam them one after the other.
Set the plate on the rack, turn the heat down to medium so the water simmers, and cover. Steam for 7 to 10 minutes for fillets about 1 inch thick, or 4 to 5 minutes for thin ones.

Press a table knife into the thickest part. It's done when the knife slides in with no resistance and the fish is white all the way through and flakes. If it isn't, cover it and steam for 1 to 2 minutes. Overcooked fish turns tough.
Turn off the heat, lift the plate out with oven mitts and carefully pour off the liquid that's collected around the fish.

Heat 1/4 cup of the oil in a small saucepan or wok over medium high. Add the ginger that isn't on the side plate and fry it for 1 minute, until it smells strong and the edges turn golden. Add the rest of the scallions and cilantro that aren't on the side plate. They'll sizzle.
Pour in the soy mixture and let it bubble for about 30 seconds, until the scallions and cilantro just wilt. Spoon it all over the fish.
Scatter the reserved raw scallions, ginger and cilantro over the top.
Heat the last 2 tbsp oil in the same pan until it shimmers. Pour it over the raw scallions and ginger. Stand back a little. It will sizzle and spit.
Taste a flake of fish with some of the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: All three steam white fish on a plate over simmering water, pour off the steaming liquid, and finish it with ginger and scallion and hot oil poured over until it sizzles. The Woks of Life (the lead) steams fillets for 7 to 10 minutes, fries two thirds of the ginger, scallion and cilantro in oil, bubbles them with a thin mix of light soy, hot water, salt and sugar and pours that over, with an extra splash of hot oil on the raw third as an option. RecipeTin Eats steams whole bream or snapper with a splash of sake, then tops it with raw ginger and shallot, soy and sesame oil and pours hot oil over; Omnivore's Cookbook steams flounder under a black bean sauce before the hot oil goes on. This one follows the lead for 4 and includes the hot oil finish.
